justifications.functional_suitability: All requirements are met: Scoring Engine Container evaluates transactions (R-01), Case Management Backend and UI handle analyst reviews (R-02), and Rule & Model Distribution Service enables dynamic hot-reloading without downtime (R-03).
justifications.performance_efficiency: The sub-50ms P99 target at 3,000 TPS is well supported by high-performance Rust in the Wasm Execution Runtime, low-latency Amazon ElastiCache Redis feature lookups, and asynchronous offloading via Audit Writer Sidecar.
justifications.compatibility: Interoperability is thoroughly addressed with standardized interfaces: gRPC and HTTPS for Payment Processor Systems, OIDC for the Identity Provider, and native AWS SDK/REST integrations for S3 and SageMaker Model Registry.
justifications.usability: Fraud analysts and compliance officers are directly served by the Case Management UI, featuring specialized components including Case Workspace, Queue Analytics, and an Audit & Explainability View powered by D3.js.
justifications.reliability: While Audit Writer Sidecar provides local ring buffering and DLQs, the architecture lacks an explicit fallback, circuit breaker, or fail-open mechanism in AWS API Gateway / Envoy to prevent blocking payments during scoring outages (R-07).
justifications.security: Security is robust: Wasm Tokenization Engine strips cardholder data at ingress, AWS KMS CMK encrypts data at rest, mTLS protects internal transit, and QLDB/S3 Object Lock ensures 7-year immutable, tamper-evident audit records.
justifications.maintainability: Modular domain separation and managed AWS services reduce operational burden for three engineers. However, managing a polyglot stack across Rust, Go, Python, and TypeScript creates maintenance friction for a small team.
justifications.portability: The design deploys cleanly into AWS eu-west-1 using ECS Fargate, Lambda, and S3, though deep coupling with proprietary services like Amazon QLDB and AWS KMS limits migration or multi-cloud portability.

PERF-01.justification: Rust/Go scoring runtime with in-memory Redis feature lookups and asynchronous audit dispatch ensures hot path execution finishes well within 50 ms at 3,000 TPS.
tradeoffs: In-memory feature storage increases infrastructure cost to meet strict P99 latency

PERF-02.justification: Complete decoupling of Case Management (Aurora PostgreSQL) from the synchronous scoring path (Rust/Redis) prevents analyst workload contention, preserving sub-50ms scoring and sub-2s case loading.
sensitivity_points: Database read capacity on Aurora PostgreSQL under heavy analyst query load
tradeoffs: Data duplication between operational scoring datastores and case management relational storage

AVAIL-01.justification: No fallback scoring logic or circuit-breaker routing is defined in API Gateway/Envoy or Scoring Engine to decide payments when the engine crashes.
sensitivity_points: Lack of circuit-breaker fallback routing at ingress layer
tradeoffs: Omitting stand-in fallback logic simplifies edge proxies but risks payment blocking on engine failure

AVAIL-02.justification: Asynchronous audit dispatch to a dedicated sidecar with mmap ring buffering and DLQ decouples scoring from audit store degradation, guaranteeing zero record loss and stable latency.
sensitivity_points: Local disk buffer capacity during sustained audit store outages
tradeoffs: Asynchronous buffering risks small lag in audit durability to protect scoring latency

MOD-01.justification: Hot-reloading of verified Wasm artifacts via Rule & Model Distribution Service enables zero-downtime model deployments, rapid rollback, and explicit tracking of model versions in decision logs.
sensitivity_points: Atomic reloading of Wasm execution runtime without dropping in-flight requests
tradeoffs: Compiling models to Wasm adds build complexity but enables safe zero-downtime hot reloading

MOD-02.justification: Wasm rules are validated, compiled, and hot-reloaded dynamically into the scoring runtime, while decision payloads log applied rules and features without service restarts.
sensitivity_points: Rule validation and compilation pipeline latency
tradeoffs: Compiling rules through a formal validation pipeline slows publication slightly but guarantees runtime safety

SEC-01.justification: Wasm tokenization prevents card number exposure to analysts, but automated anomalous analyst behavior detection and 15-minute alerting mechanisms are not architected in the case management components.
sensitivity_points: Absence of behavioral anomaly detection and rapid alerting mechanisms
tradeoffs: Early edge tokenization reduces PCI-DSS scope across internal services

SEC-02.justification: S3 Object Lock in Compliance Mode paired with QLDB cryptographic ledger preserves immutable decision metadata, inputs, and explanations for 7 years, enabling rapid compliance retrieval.
sensitivity_points: Retention policy enforcement and index efficiency over long-term archive
tradeoffs: Dual-storage in QLDB and S3 Object Lock increases complexity and cost for immutable auditability
